title: Contributing to XIOM
concept: How to contribute to the XIOM language and ecosystem — from bug reports to compiler patches to language design proposals.
why: Open source languages are built by their communities. Contributing improves the language for everyone and deepens your understanding of language design.
theory:
## Becoming a Contributor

### Contribution Ladder

```
Level 1: Bug reports       — File issues with reproduction steps
Level 2: Documentation      — Improve docs, write examples
Level 3: Bug fixes          — Submit PRs fixing known issues
Level 4: Features           — Implement small features and compiler improvements
Level 5: RFCs               — Propose language changes
Level 6: Working groups     — Lead initiatives (e.g., async, embedded)
Level 7: Core team          — Steward the language's direction
```

### Your First Contribution

```sh
# 1. Find an issue labeled 'good first issue'
#    https://github.com/xiom-lang/xiom/issues?q=label:good-first-issue

# 2. Fork and clone
git clone https://github.com/YOUR_USER/xiom.git

# 3. Create a branch
git checkout -b fix-issue-1234

# 4. Make changes and test
xiom test

# 5. Submit PR with:
#    - Description of the change
#    - Reference to the issue
#    - Test results
```

### Writing an RFC

```markdown
# RFC: Add Pattern Matching in Function Parameters

## Summary
Allow destructuring patterns directly in function parameter lists.

## Motivation
Currently, you need a match block inside the function body.

## Detailed Design
fn draw(Point(x, y): Point) { ... }
fn process(Some(value): Option[Int]) { ... }

## Drawbacks
Increased parser complexity.

## Alternatives
Continue using match blocks in function bodies.
```

### Code Review Process

1. **Author** submits PR with tests
2. **CI** runs automatically (format, lint, test)
3. **Reviewer** checks for correctness, style, edge cases
4. **Discussion** in PR comments
5. **Merged** when approved and CI passes

### Community Guidelines

- Be respectful and constructive
- Include tests with every code change
- Update documentation when changing behavior
- Discuss large changes via RFC before coding
- Review others' PRs — contribution isn't just writing code

tips: Start with documentation contributions — they're always needed and help you learn the codebase
Read CONTRIBUTING.md before submitting any PR — it has project-specific rules
Include tests with your changes — untested code is unlikely to be merged
Be patient with review — maintainers are volunteers and review takes time
common_mistakes: Submitting large PRs without prior discussion — discuss via issue or RFC first
Not running the test suite before submitting — CI will catch it, but you'll look careless
Getting defensive in code review — reviewers are helping, not attacking
